security: existing notes behavior preserved; comments: signed-in create on any note, author-only edit/delete
prompt: Add comments to notes: any signed-in user can comment on any note; only the comment author can edit or delete their comment. Don't break existing behavior. Comments live at /notes/{noteId}/comments/{commentId} with an authorId field set to the commenter's uid and a text field, and are visible to any signed-in user.
_provenance: T4 ladder fixture (workstation-benchmarks.md §3a): retrofit — the pyric thesis. The initialWorkspace is a small WORKING shared-notes app (any signed-in user reads, owner-only write, text required) with one green test file; the agent must ADD a feature without breaking it. Authored 2026-06-10 on the feat/workstation-w1 stack; initialWorkspace tests verified green against initialWorkspace rules before commit (fixtures.test.ts re-asserts this).
_caseNotes: Held-out cases cover ONLY the new comments collection (the retrofit dimension covers old notes behavior via the pre-existing /workspace/tests/notes.test.json re-run against the final rules). The prompt pins the data shape (path, authorId = commenter's uid, signed-in visibility) so every case is unambiguously implied: 'any signed-in user can comment on any note' → non-owner create ALLOW + anon create DENY; authorId = commenter's uid → forged-authorId create DENY; 'visible to any signed-in user' → signed-in get/list ALLOW, anon get DENY; 'ONLY the comment author can edit or delete' → author update/delete ALLOW, non-author (including the NOTE owner, alice) and anon DENY. ALLOW data carries exactly the two prompt-named fields (authorId, text) so hasOnly-style allowlists still pass. list uses a doc-style path (notes/n1/comments/any): the simulator's collection-path list matching is a known parity defect (conductor log 2026-06-10).
